security_audit.summary: Most static backtick, URL, filesystem, and environment-file alerts are documentation false positives. Real issues remain in dynamic exec examples, comment-triggered workflows, GITHUB_TOKEN usage, and untrusted GitHub content passed into shell commands and AI prompts.

remediation.issue: Dynamic shell command construction in git helper examples
remediation.suggestion: Use argument-array process execution, validate commit hashes and branch names, and avoid interpolated shell strings.

remediation.issue: Raw GitHub event text interpolated into shell commands
remediation.suggestion: Pass event data through environment variables or files, quote safely, and use multiline-safe GITHUB_OUTPUT syntax.

remediation.issue: Comment-triggered commands can perform repository write operations
remediation.suggestion: Require collaborator permission checks, restrict triggers to trusted actors, and set explicit job permissions.

remediation.issue: Untrusted content is sent directly to AI prompts
remediation.suggestion: Add prompt-injection boundaries, validate model output, and require human approval before mutating repository state.

semantic_findings.title: Comment Body Shell Injection in Mention Bot
semantic_findings.description: The mention bot workflow places github.event.comment.body inside a shell command before writing QUESTION. A crafted issue comment can break quoting and run commands in the workflow runner.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow is triggered by issue comments and interpolates the raw comment body into shell. This is a known GitHub Actions script injection pattern.

semantic_findings.title: Comment Triggered Rebase Can Mutate Branches
semantic_findings.description: The auto-rebase workflow runs on any issue comment containing /rebase, then checks out, rebases, and force-pushes with GITHUB_TOKEN. It does not show an actor permission or association check.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The trigger condition only checks comment content and pull request presence. The shown job then uses a repository token for write-sensitive git operations.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Content Sent Directly to AI Prompts
semantic_findings.description: PR diffs, issue bodies, deployment changes, and bot context are inserted into AI prompts without prompt-injection boundaries or output validation. Attackers can influence labels, comments, or deployment decisions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Multiple workflows place repository or user-controlled content directly into AI instructions. The resulting AI output can drive labels, comments, and deployment decisions.

content.value_statement: GitHub automation is hard to maintain when reviews, triage, and release checks spread across workflows. This skill provides reusable AI-assisted GitHub Actions patterns for review, triage, deployment checks, and repository maintenance.
actual_capabilities: Provides GitHub Actions examples for AI pull request review and issue triage.
Shows workflow patterns for stale issue handling, rollback, branch cleanup, and branch protection.
Includes CI/CD examples for smart test selection and deployment risk assessment.
Covers git operations such as rebasing, cherry-picking, and branch maintenance.
Defines prompt structures for review comments, issue classification, and AI assistant responses.
Lists security, performance, and reliability checks for GitHub automation.
limitations: Examples require security review and hardening before production use.
Several helper functions are illustrative and are not complete implementations.
The skill does not enforce authorization checks for bot commands.
Users must configure GitHub secrets, permissions, runners, and provider API access.

use_cases.title: Add AI Pull Request Review
use_cases.description: Create a workflow that summarizes pull request changes and posts structured review feedback.

use_cases.title: Automate Issue Triage
use_cases.description: Classify new issues, suggest labels, and request missing reproduction details from reporters.

use_cases.title: Coordinate CI/CD Decisions
use_cases.description: Use change analysis, targeted tests, deployment risk checks, and rollback patterns in release workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Create PR Review Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a GitHub Actions workflow that uses Claude to summarize pull request changes and post review comments. Include required permissions and secrets.

prompt_templates.title: Add Issue Triage Rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan an AI issue triage workflow for my repository. Include label categories, maintainer review points, and safe default behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Harden Bot Commands
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my comment-triggered GitHub bot workflow. Identify authorization checks, token permissions, input handling, and logging changes needed before deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Design Secure CI/CD Gates
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a secure AI-assisted CI/CD workflow using Codex or Claude Code. Include test selection, deployment risk review, rollback steps, and manual approvals.

output_examples.input: Assess a pull request review workflow for a small TypeScript project.
output: Summary of the review flow and required provider secrets.
Permission recommendations for pull request comments.
Risks to fix before enabling the workflow.

output_examples.input: Plan issue triage automation for an open source repository.
output: Suggested label groups for bugs, features, questions, and documentation.
A maintainer review step for uncertain classifications.

output_examples.input: Review a comment-triggered GitHub bot command.
output: Safe handling for comment text and workflow outputs.
Token and permission limits for the workflow.

best_practices: Set the smallest GitHub token permissions needed for each workflow job.
Treat issue text, comments, branch names, and pull request content as untrusted input.
Require human approval before AI output changes code, branches, labels, or deployments.
anti_patterns: Do not interpolate raw GitHub event fields directly into shell commands.
Do not allow public comments to trigger write operations without authorization checks.
Do not send sensitive code, secrets, or private deployment data to AI providers without approval.

faq.question: Does this skill create workflows automatically?
faq.answer: It provides patterns and prompts that an AI assistant can adapt into workflow files.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Are the examples production ready?
faq.answer: No. Review permissions, inputs, secrets, and approval gates before using them in production.

faq.question: Does it require GitHub Actions?
faq.answer: Most examples target GitHub Actions, GitHub Script, GitHub CLI, and the GitHub REST API.

faq.question: Can it replace human code review?
faq.answer: No. Use it to assist reviewers, summarize changes, and highlight risks for human decisions.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Store provider keys and GitHub tokens in GitHub Secrets, and restrict workflow permissions per job.
